entityDescription:
Science Foundation Ireland's research promotes and assists the development and competitiveness of industry, enterprise and employment in Ireland. Oriented basic research is research that is carried out with the expectation that it will produce a broad base of knowledge that is likely to form the background to the solution of recognised, or expected, current or future problems or possibilities.
Applied research is an original investigation undertaken to acquire new knowledge and is directed primarily towards a specific practical aim or objective. The results of applied research are intended primarily to be valid for a single or limited number of products, operations, methods, or systems.
SFI also promotes and supports the study of, education in, and engagement with STEM and promotes an awareness and understanding of the value of STEM to society and, in particular, to the growth of the economy. The definition of STEM employed by SFI does not extend to the Humanities and Social Sciences, except where it may pertain to the specific mission of the Foundation – for example, through the use of targeted instruments, SFI may support the development, assessment and publication of research to assess the impact of funded research activities, STEM teaching, etc.

entityDescription:
Gdansk University of Technology GUT was founded in 1904. It is the largest technical university in Northern Poland, and one of the most prestigious and widely recognized internationally. At present, nearly 22,000 students are enrolled at 9 faculties, 7 of which posses the highest rank A category. The university employs 2,800 staff including over 1,300 academics. According to the Ministry of Science and Higher Education most secondary-school graduates willing to undertake technical studies in Poland chose GUT. 
University posses modern R&D infrastructure, including among others HRPT/MetOp satellite ground station, Peta flop class cluster for big data processing and Full size cubic Cave Automatic Virtual Environment laboratory.
In the last year GUT obtained prestigious HR Excellence in Research logo given by European Commission, and as one of the 12 best Polish universities was qualified to The Times Higher Education World University Rankings.
The university continually strives to ensure that at least 20% of graduates establish their own high tech start-up companies, mostly in Information and Communications Technology (ICT) and chemistry.
In the academic year 2016/2017 the new intercollegiate field of study Space and Satellite Technology was established at GUT jointly with Maritime University and the Naval Academy in Gdynia.
Gdansk – where the university is located – is one of the most beautiful Polish cities on the Baltic Sea Coast. It is in Gdansk that SOLIDARITY movement was born. It eventually led to the fall of the Berlin Wall and initiates a Europe unification process.

entityDescription:
Trueflaw produces cracks using natural thermal fatigue damage mechanism. The produced natural cracks have similar properties to most service induced cracks. There are no changes to the microstructure of the sample or other artifacts induced by the process. Cracks can be produced to various materials and complex shapes. Crack sizes range from below 0.1 mm to 100 mm and above. Samples of any size can be handled.

The cracks are produced with fully automated crack making machines. Process is highly repeatable. Crack depth information is available through destructive validation of simplified sample. We currently have 10 crack making machines working 24/7 so we can work on several cracks parallel. We have made 2906 cracks to date.

entityDescription: Polish Space Industry Association (SPACE PL) was founded in 31 October, 2012. Currently has more than 70 Polish associated companies and research institutes which operate in the space sector. SPACE PL mission is to create a strong Polish space industry that will successfully compete on the European space market. Its main objective is to consolidate the business community, research centers and organizations interested in space exploration and scientific research and implementation of products and technologies for space applications. Polish Space Industry Association improves the economic potential of the space industry and initiates cooperation between Polish actors of the space sector and related sectors (aviation, defense). Purpose for that is to efficiently utilize funds from the state budget, available programs from the European Space Agency (ESA) and the European Union. SPACE PL cares about entrepreneurs demands and its effective use by institutions and public organizations to space policy. Therefore, one of the goals of SPACE PL is reinforcing general cooperation and collaboration on the process of creating a national space policy with the Sejm (the lower house of the Polish Parliament) and Senate of Poland, the Council of Ministers, ministries, Polish Space Agency and other state administration representatives. Polish Space Industry Association also initiates and co-operates and reinforce relations between the business and science business space sector.

Clients are Governmental Institutions (both central and local); public companies; consul-tancy firms; research centers and socio-economic research institutes; pharmaceutical companies; wholesale distribution organisa-tions; telecommunication, insurance, banking and financial firms.

Services provided include:
¿	Design and implementation of Geographic Information Systems and database
¿	Design and implementation of corporate database
¿	Geographic and corporate data integration
¿	Data collection and processing
¿	Customized development of application models and procedures
¿	Software development
¿	Training (in classrooms or at the Client¿s place) 
¿	Customer care and technical assistance
¿	Consultancy.

GIS development activities are primarily addressed to meet the Public Administration needs and constitute the necessary support for drawing regional development plans and urban physical plans.
Such support is mainly provided by converting high-scale cartography from CAD to GIS format, setting up of topographical bases in raster format, developing geographic data bank in vector shape for use in environmental mapping, land register, risk maps, land use maps, physical atlas, structural plans, etc.


BI development activities are primarily addressed to meet the needs of large and medium-size firms and are constituted by developing Data Warehouses and OLAP tools to access those data. Such system types are mainly utilised to support decisions processes. 
The Data Warehousing process is imple¬mented using the SAS system.

By integrating geographic and corporate data, Sistemi Territoriali develops geomarketing applications involving: demographic analysis, consumption patterns¿ analysis, customers¿ geocoding, and interactive mapping for Internet.

Sistemi Territoriali also develops multimedia applica¬tions for Internet or CD.

Sistemi Territoriali technical services are complemented by educational services which assure its Clients¿ full comprehension of the technology provided and easy installation / use of the systems provided. Moreover, by enlarging and strengthening its Clients¿ capabilities, Sistemi Territoriali contributes to a balanced growth of the market.

Sistemi Territoriali also carries briefing courses concerning GIS and vocational sessions for the use of software products. Training courses to ArcGIS are carried by personnel qualified as ¿ESRI Inc Certified Instructors¿.
SAS Institute employs Sistemi Territoriali¿s personnel to carry out training courses on various subjects regarding application development of Executive Information Systems (EIS).
Sistemi Territoriali is a Business Partner of ESRI Italia ® and Partner of SAS ® Institute.

entityDescription:
EICAS AUTOMAZIONE S.p.A. has a long-standing heritage in the field of attitude determination using star measurements. Building on experience gained from the HIPPARCOS mission, the company has designed and validated numerous Autonomous Attitude Determination Systems (AADS) under ESA/ASI contracts and for major aerospace players. These systems have evolved from single-head to multi-head and multi-camera configurations, and from CCD to CMOS sensor technologies.
In recent years, EICAS has developed a new, cost-effective multicamera system architecture featuring advanced in-flight auto-calibration techniques. These techniques enable precise calibration of both the camera model and the camera's orientation with respect to the spacecraft reference frame.
The company’s first proprietary star tracker, ARGO 1.0, was successfully validated in orbit, completing an extensive In-Orbit Demonstration (IOD) campaign from January 2021 to July 2022 onboard ION-mk02 by D-ORBIT S.p.A. Its development was co-funded by the H2020 SME Instrument Programme.
A second star tracker, ARGO 2.0, was developed under the ESA Competitiveness & Growth (C&G) Programme. Designed specifically for the constellation market, ARGO 2.0 features a significantly reduced size, weight, and power (SWaP) footprint. Full on-ground qualification campaign was completed in 2023. The in-orbit validation is scheduled for 2026.

Company description: EICAS AUTOMAZIONE S.p.A. has a long-standing heritage in the field of attitude determination using star measurements. Building on experience gained from the HIPPARCOS mission, the company has designed and validated numerous Autonomous Attitude Determination Systems (AADS) under ESA/ASI contracts and for major aerospace players. These systems have evolved from single-head to multi-head and multi-camera configurations, and from CCD to CMOS sensor technologies.
In recent years, EICAS has developed a new, cost-effective multicamera system architecture featuring advanced in-flight auto-calibration techniques. These techniques enable precise calibration of both the camera model and the camera's orientation with respect to the spacecraft reference frame.
The company’s first proprietary star tracker, ARGO 1.0, was successfully validated in orbit, completing an extensive In-Orbit Demonstration (IOD) campaign from January 2021 to July 2022 onboard ION-mk02 by D-ORBIT S.p.A. Its development was co-funded by the H2020 SME Instrument Programme.
A second star tracker, ARGO 2.0, was developed under the ESA Competitiveness & Growth (C&G) Programme. Designed specifically for the constellation market, ARGO 2.0 features a significantly reduced size, weight, and power (SWaP) footprint. Full on-ground qualification campaign was completed in 2023. The in-orbit validation is scheduled for 2026.
